chapter: Looking back and the lean years
title: California with no work, awards without jobs, and the 1967 collapse
summary: He goes three months without work, plays a boxing match, wins awards but cannot book the best band in California, and in 1967 gets an ulcer before touring England.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: And, it was very expensive to do this, to get the jobs I went back for. You're talking about the time I went to California and had the great band which I had many times --
Yeah.

-- that's in the same period of time that I just told you about the guy that wanted three guys out of six--- well, in that period, we had a nice apartment - we didn't buy a house at this point; but, we had a hell of a nice apartment - all furnished and lovely and, uh, I went as far in that period of having three months without working at all; and the only thing I did then was to keep my chops going would be to jump in the car and go where I knew some guys were playing and sat in and keep my lip up and such things as that. That is pretty bad. And, there was no single jobs. I remember once doing such things as playing at a boxing match of all things for such a good band to do. You know, and getting very little money doing it.
Shades of the Ohio Lucky Seven.

Yeah - damn near - yeah. But, uh, at that time, in California there was absolutely nothing. There was nothing; a few little joints having a five-piece band - a four-piece band on Saturdays and Sundays paying no

money and they would pay scale only and there is no musician in California that I know that can live on scale; the union scales at that time were so low that it was like picking up pin money, youknow, cigarette money over the weekend.
Well, do you remember getting recognition at that time from a couple of jazz clubs and some magazine for your musicial ability - for your cornet playing.
Well, I've had lots of those things---
Well, at that specific time you got them and you couldn't get a job --
Well, I said the same thing -- I had the best band in California and couldn't book it.
Yeah. But, it's the irony of getting awards and no work - it's kind of weird.
Well, the music business is kind of weird -- ---
That was 1967 and that's when you ended up at the end of the summer getting ill, right?
Well, I got an ulcer and my wife said I damn near died but I guess maybe I did. It didn't seem to me that I was dying though at that time.
Well, you didn't.
No. I beat that rap --
And in three weeks you were back on the road--
Well, I went to England after that.
Yeah.
Yes.
Okay.
